Einar Paz
PhD Student in Economics
The University of Texas at Austin
EmailCVLinkedIn


Welcome! I am a PhD student in Economics at The University of Texas at Austin.
My research interests are in macroeconomics, behavioral macroeconomics, and monetary economics. In particular, I study how households and firms form expectations, and how these beliefs shape macroeconomic dynamics and the transmission of monetary policy.

Research fields
Macroeconomics · Behavioral Macroeconomics · Monetary Economics

title: Research
text:
The Prices That Shape Household Inflation Expectations


Work in progress




Rational Inattention in Wage Growth Expectations


Working paper

Abstract
Using data from the New York Fed’s Survey of Consumer Expectations, I document that wage growth expectations display highly anchored and unresponsive behavior, even during inflationary episodes in which inflation expectations respond strongly. To explain these patterns, I develop a rational inattention framework embedded in an otherwise standard New Keynesian model with price and wage rigidities. The economy is subject to two structural shocks: a cost-push shock that raises inflation while reducing wage growth, and a wage-markup shock that increases both. Households optimally observe a single noisy signal that is a linear combination of the two shocks. Because both shocks raise prices, households’ expectations of inflation respond in the standard attenuated fashion typical of rational inattention. However, because the two shocks have opposite implications for wage growth and households cannot disentangle their contributions, their inferred effects on expected wage growth partially offset each other, producing muted and unresponsive wage growth expectations consistent with the survey evidence.

Presentations

Economics Graduate Student Conference, Washington University in St. Louis, 2026
Midwest Macroeconomics Meetings, Texas Tech University, 2026





Inflation and Unemployment in Household Expectations: Evidence from German Households


with Anushka Mitra and Prachi Srivastava


Work in progress

Abstract
This project investigates how households perceive the relationship between inflation and unemployment, motivated by a puzzling pattern in the ECB Consumer Expectations Survey (CES): households expecting higher inflation also tend to expect higher unemployment. This positive association contrasts with the conventional Phillips-curve relationship and raises questions about the economic mechanisms underlying households’ beliefs. To investigate these perceptions, we designed a randomized survey experiment embedded in the Bundesbank Online Panel – Households (BOP-HH), combining hypothetical inflation scenarios with questions on the mechanisms and narratives shaping respondents’ beliefs. The questionnaire module was approved and implemented by the Deutsche Bundesbank in October 2026, providing the basis for new evidence on how households understand the relationship between inflation and unemployment.
